content.title: Finger Control | Four-Axis Same-Beat Full-Body Response
content.summary: Keep a small foreground controller and a complete responder readable in one continuous frame. Map up, down, left, and right to fixed full-body responses, execute one cue and one matching response per beat, repeat both axes to prove the rule, then allow one brief release.

quick_start.input_format: Stable continuous take + co-visible foreground controller and complete responder + fixed four-direction mapping + one command and one same-beat full-body response per beat + repeated vertical and horizontal axis tests + one brief final release
quick_start.recommended_input: In a bright robotics laboratory, a light-gray-gloved technician keeps only a small luminous stylus in the lower-right foreground. An original full-size robot follows the ten-beat sequence UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT, LEFT, RIGHT, UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT with synchronized rises, lowers, or full-body lateral shifts, then ends with one amber light pulse and arm lift.
required_anchors: 第一条指令前，控制器和完整响应者已经同框且都可读。
屏幕方向固定：上=升、下=降、左=整体左移、右=整体右移。
每个指令只对应一个同拍响应；无提前、延迟、轴向翻转或独立即兴。
横向是可见全身位移，纵向改变重心；纵横轴都至少重复一次再收尾。
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Keep a small foreground controller and a complete responder readable in one continuous frame. Map up, down, left, and right to fixed full-body responses, execute one cue and one matching response per beat, repeat both axes to prove the rule, then allow one brief release.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: A visible foreground controller establishes a fixed four-direction screen-space language; a co-visible responder begins one matching full-body movement within the same beat for every cue, and repeated axis alternation lets the audience learn and verify the causal rule inside one continuous frame.

invariants.rule: The visible controller and full responder must be co-visible before the first command and remain jointly readable throughout.
invariants.ablation_failure: If either party leaves frame or the hand covers the responder, the audience cannot verify causality and the hook becomes an ordinary dance or mime.

invariants.rule: Use one fixed screen-coordinate mapping: up means rise, down means lower, left means shift left and right means shift right.
invariants.ablation_failure: If axes invert, rotate or change meaning, the learned visual rule collapses and repeated commands feel random.

invariants.rule: Each deliberate cue receives one immediate beat-level response; the responder does not freestyle between commands.
invariants.ablation_failure: Delay, anticipation or unrelated choreography breaks the controller illusion even when individual poses look attractive.

invariants.rule: Horizontal commands produce whole-body displacement and vertical commands change center of gravity, keeping response amplitude unmistakable.
invariants.ablation_failure: Tiny wrist, shoulder or hip twitches are too ambiguous to read as directional control.

invariants.rule: Alternate and repeat both axes in one continuous take, then end with a brief release only after the rule has been proven.
invariants.ablation_failure: A single demonstration cannot teach and verify the mapping; cuts or an early freestyle ending remove the proof.

slots.name: responder
slots.description: Adult performer, original robot, puppet or other clearly readable full-body responder.

slots.name: controller
slots.description: Finger, stylus, baton, wand or other small foreground directional instrument.

slots.name: setting
slots.description: Room, studio, lab, stage or miniature theatre with a stable spatial baseline.

slots.name: command_sequence
slots.description: A beat-aligned order containing vertical and horizontal commands with at least one repeated axis test.

slots.name: response_vocabulary
slots.description: Rise/lower center-of-gravity changes plus visible full-body left/right shifts.

slots.name: camera
slots.description: One continuous view that preserves both cue and response; angle and lens may change by instantiation.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.description: Original beat or diegetic cue family that clearly marks each command without copying source audio.

slots.name: release
slots.description: A brief final flourish after the mapping has been proven.

anti_copy_exclusions: Do not reproduce the source woman's face, hairstyle, body proportions or recognizable likeness.
Do not reproduce the black cutout bodysuit or its exact silhouette.
Do not reproduce the source blue-gray room, wall-mounted television, door placement, ceiling-light layout or floor arrangement.
Do not reproduce the source foreground hand's exact appearance, scale path or framing errors.
Do not reuse the exact observed dance surface, exact source command timing or source audio; preserve only the abstract causal grammar.

instantiations.concept: Luminous stylus controls a studio robot
instantiations.description: In a bright robotics lab, a gloved technician's lower-right luminous stylus directs an original full-size articulated studio robot through the same four-axis response grammar in one uncut take.

instantiations.concept: Conductor baton controls an adult mime
instantiations.description: On a white cyc stage, a small foreground conductor baton directs an original adult mime in a saffron rehearsal outfit through rise, lower and full-body side shifts without musical freelancing.

instantiations.concept: Magnetic wand controls a paper puppet
instantiations.description: In a handcrafted tabletop theatre, a foreground magnetic wand directs a large articulated paper puppet through the same four screen-direction responses while both remain visible.

failure_modes.failure: The controller crosses the center or covers the responder.
failure_modes.repair: Keep the controller inside a reserved foreground quadrant and cap its apparent area before rendering.

failure_modes.failure: The responder uses tiny ambiguous twitches.
failure_modes.repair: Require visible center-of-gravity change for vertical cues and whole-body displacement for horizontal cues.

failure_modes.failure: The responder anticipates, lags or freestyles.
failure_modes.repair: Use one cue per beat, start cue and response together, and prohibit unrelated movement between commands.

failure_modes.failure: The camera or responder scale drifts until one party becomes unreadable.
failure_modes.repair: Lock a continuous framing corridor and keep both controller and responder legible for all commands.

failure_modes.failure: Left/right mapping flips across the take.
failure_modes.repair: Define screen coordinates once and restate them as a hard continuity constraint.
Reduce the vocabulary to rise, lower and full-body side shifts; reserve one flourish for the final release.

transfer_tests.concept: Luminous stylus controls a studio robot
transfer_tests.finding: The mapping stays legible with a nonhuman responder and new industrial surface; the hook does not depend on the source dancer, wardrobe or room.

transfer_tests.concept: Conductor baton controls an adult mime
transfer_tests.finding: A stage-performance transfer preserves the controller-responder proof while changing costume, palette, instrument and performance genre.

review.method: canonical-source English editorial pass with terminology, identity, and stable-token validation
